title: JuiceFS / Mount clients
description: Client side of JuiceFS, scraped from the CSI mount pods. Note that all mount pods share one cache dir on disk: cache size gauges are aggregated with max(), traffic counters with sum(). Counters restart from zero whenever a mount process restarts (a redeploy, a cache-dir change, or an OOM kill), so everything here is rate()/increase() rather than a raw counter.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio (bytes)
panels.description: Share of read bytes served from the local block cache over the dashboard's time range. Everything missing is fetched from S3. Counters restart from zero whenever a mount process restarts (a redeploy, a cache-dir change, or an OOM kill), so everything here is rate()/increase() rather than a raw counter.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio (blocks)
panels.description: Same ratio counted in block reads instead of bytes; diverges from the byte ratio when misses are unusually large or small blocks.

panels.title: S3 GET requests
panels.description: Object storage GETs issued by the mounts over the time range. This is the line item on the AWS bill, both per-request and per-byte.

panels.title: Bytes read from S3
panels.description: Block cache misses over the time range, i.e. bytes that had to come from object storage. Tracks the GET count above.

panels.title: Cached data on disk
panels.description: Bytes currently in the block cache. storageClassShareMount is false, so every PVC gets its own mount pod, but all of them point at the same JuiceFS volume and the same cache-dir on disk. Each pod reports the whole shared cache as its own, so summing this across pods multiplies it by the number of mounts — it is aggregated with max() on purpose.

panels.title: Shortest mount uptime
panels.description: Time since the youngest mount process started. A small value means at least one mount restarted recently and its counters are back at zero.

panels.title: Block cache reads/s
panels.description: Block reads served from the local cache versus reads that fell through to object storage. Per-mount traffic, so these are summed.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio by volume
panels.description: Byte hit ratio per volume. All volumes share one cache dir, so a volume with heavy cold reads evicts blocks the others were relying on.

panels.title: Cached bytes on disk
panels.description: Size of the shared block cache. storageClassShareMount is false, so every PVC gets its own mount pod, but all of them point at the same JuiceFS volume and the same cache-dir on disk. Each pod reports the whole shared cache as its own, so summing this across pods multiplies it by the number of mounts — it is aggregated with max() on purpose. The dashed line is the configured cache-size (30GiB); juicefs also keeps free-space-ratio headroom, so it settles below that.

panels.title: Cache evictions & drops/s
panels.description: Evictions are the cache making room and are normal once it is full; drops are blocks the cache refused to write at all. Sustained evictions next to a falling hit ratio means the working set no longer fits.

panels.title: Object requests/s by method
panels.description: Requests the mounts send to S3. GET is a cache miss being paid for; PUT is new data being uploaded after upload-delay.

panels.title: Object request errors/s
panels.description: Failed requests to object storage. Anything sustained here means reads are failing or writes are stuck retrying.

panels.title: Object request latency, p99
panels.description: 99th percentile round trip to S3 per method. Read latency here is what a cache miss actually costs the application in wall time.

panels.title: S3 GETs/s by volume
panels.description: Which volume is driving object storage reads. Per-mount traffic, safe to sum.

panels.title: FUSE throughput
panels.description: Bytes the applications actually read and write through the mount, before the cache and object storage below it.

panels.title: FUSE ops/s by volume
panels.description: Filesystem operations per second per volume — how busy each mount is.

panels.title: FUSE I/O errors/s
panels.description: Errors returned to applications, by errno. ENOENT is ordinary lookup noise; anything else is worth reading the mount log for.

panels.title: Staging blocks pending upload
panels.description: Blocks written locally and not yet uploaded, held back by upload-delay=10s. A backlog that keeps growing means uploads are not keeping up with writes.

panels.title: Mount process memory
panels.description: Memory each mount process reports. The 1Gi limit is per mount pod; immich's mount was OOM killed 25 times in 38h before the limit was raised, and every kill zeroed its counters.

panels.title: Mount uptime
panels.description: Time since each mount process started. A sawtooth here is a restart, and every restart resets the counters on this dashboard — read drops to zero as a restart, not an outage.
